title: Microsoft Purview: per-policy coverage report for auto-labeling

claims.claim: The roadmap record was modified at 2026-11-11T00:52:46.
Microsoft Purview Information Protection is gaining a per-policy coverage report for auto-labeling.
claims.quote: We're introducing a new coverage report for Microsoft Purview Information Protection auto-labeling policies.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report compares policy enforcement with the most recent simulation.
claims.quote: For each enforced auto-labeling policy, admins can view how files processed during enforcement correlate to the latest simulation run.

claims.claim: The report shows successfully labeled files.
claims.quote: Review files that were successfully labeled during enforcement.

claims.claim: The report shows files still being processed.
claims.quote: The report provides a centralized view of files that were successfully labeled, files that are still being processed, and files that require attention.

claims.claim: The report identifies unsuccessful label applications.
claims.quote: Investigate files where label application was unsuccessful.

claims.quote: Update internal operational documentation for administrators who monitor auto-labeling policy effectiveness.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters

claims.quote: No action is required to receive this feature.

claims.claim: Open coverage in Microsoft Purview portal through Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Coverage > View coverage.
claims.quote:
go to **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**.
2. Select an auto-labeling policy that includes SharePoint or OneDrive, has completed simulation, and is turned on.
3. In the **Coverage** column, select **View coverage**.

claims.claim: Open the newer per-policy review pages through Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**. Select a policy, then select **View details** in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -IncludeProgressFeedback retrieves policy labeling progress.
claims.quote:
Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy
    [[-Identity] <PolicyIdParameter>]
    [-DistributionDetail]
    [-ForceValidate <Boolean>]
    [-IncludeProgressFeedback]
    [-IncludeTestModeResults <Boolean>]

claims.claim: The cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The PowerShell alternative reports labeling progress for enabled policies.
claims.quote: If you use this switch, the command shows the progress of files to be labeled, files labeled in the last 7 days, and total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The documented progress command does not provide the coverage comparison with simulation.
claims.quote: Searched: coverage AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy; Purview auto-labeling coverage PowerShell Graph. Read Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy, including IncludeProgressFeedback and IncludeTestModeResults, and the feature's coverage and PowerShell sections; no comparison output is documented.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice describes monitoring enforcement outcomes rather than a new labeling action by the report.
claims.quote: This feature introduces a new coverage report that enables administrators to monitor and assess auto-labeling policy enforcement outcomes, including labeled files, pending files, and labeling failures.

claims.claim: Labeling continues to be performed by the enabled auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until they're deleted. For example, new and modified files will be included with the current policy settings.

claims.claim: The newer policy review experience has Labeled items and Labeling failures tabs.
claims.quote: The newer review page has separate **Overview**, **Labeled items**, and **Labeling failures** tabs. For policies that remove labels, the item tabs are **Label removed items** and **Label removal failures**.

claims.claim: A simulation match does not confirm that a label was applied.
claims.quote: A simulation match doesn't confirm that a label was applied.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice includes files no longer eligible for labeling because they were deleted or modified after simulation.
claims.quote: Identify files that remain pending, have not yet been processed, or are no longer eligible for labeling because they were deleted or modified after the simulation run.
